source_review.notes: Reviewed the official PostgreSQL buffer-manager design notes, current MySQL 8.4 InnoDB buffer-pool and scan-resistance documentation, the original LRU-K, 2Q, and ARC publications, and two database-systems textbooks. PostgreSQL, both MySQL pages, the 2Q paper, and the ARC page returned HTTP 200. The LRU-K DOI resolved to the correct ACM publication, whose automated-access challenge returned HTTP 403; its bibliographic identity and scoped algorithm claims were reviewed without claiming successful full-text retrieval. Vendor behavior is explicitly engine-scoped.

evidence: Checked trace r_1 through r_T, capacity C, hit/miss, LRU stack order, reuse distance, and the abstract value model V(p).
Checked distinctions among replacement ranking, admission, residency, eligibility, pins, dirty/writeback state, page identity, and ghost history.
Checked that LRU-K, 2Q, clock, scan rings, and adaptive histories are described as policy families with explicit state and scope rather than interchangeable names.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The value equation is labeled as a decision model, and all cost and probability terms require workload-specific definition.

evidence: Recomputed capacity-three LRU for A,B,C,A,D,A,B,E as 2 hits, 6 misses, evictions B,C,D, and final least-to-most order A,B,E.
Recomputed the stated one-bit clock convention as 1 hit, 7 misses, replacements A-to-D, B-to-A, C-to-B, D-to-E, and final frames E,A,B.
Recomputed exercise trace A,B,C,B,D,A,B,E: LRU has 2 hits and 6 misses; clock has 1 hit and 7 misses, final frames E,A,B, hand 1, and bits 1,0,0.
Recomputed the four-frame scan comparison: global LRU ends with S5-S8 while a two-frame hot cache plus two-frame ring retains H1,H2 and S7,S8.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Trace results use the chapter's exact initial-hand, reference-bit, insertion, and hand-advance conventions; they are not universal performance results.

evidence: Re-derived Belady's future-aware policy as an offline comparison rather than an implementable online selector.
Re-derived LRU stack order and the connection between distinct-page reuse distance and capacity-dependent LRU hits.
Re-derived the separation of policy proposal from atomic eligibility revalidation and safe frame reuse.
Re-derived how LRU-K and 2Q distinguish first touch from demonstrated recurrence using bounded history.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No competitive bound, stochastic workload law, or universal ordering of online policies is claimed.

evidence: Reviewed zero, one, empty, and full capacity; one repeated page; all-ineligible frames; saturated counters; bounded ghost history; and generation reuse.
Reviewed one-pass scans, looping scans, skewed hot sets, phase changes, prefetch error, shard imbalance, resizing, and mixed page sizes.
Reviewed pinned, dirty, loading, I/O-owned, retagged, and concurrently referenced candidates, including failed writeback and no-victim progress.
Reviewed tenant interference, hard versus soft partitions, remote-page cost asymmetry, metadata-budget fairness, and workload-specific admission.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Replacement accuracy never overrides page-lifecycle, recovery, concurrency, or durability obligations.

evidence: Validated capacity and unique-resident-page invariants in both executable policies.
Validated hits plus misses equals trace length and every reported eviction corresponds to a full-cache miss.
Validated exact LRU order, clock hand/reference transitions, two-frame ring bound, and preservation of the separate hot cache.
The repository verifier matched exact seven-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status.
invariant_checking.notes: The executable model assumes clean unpinned frames and omits concurrent eligibility, I/O, WAL, writeback, sharding, and vendor implementations.

evidence: Reviewed every LRU and clock transition in the executable and exercise traces against the stated capacity and hand convention.
Reviewed why a pinned least-recent page is ineligible even when it is the policy's top-ranked victim.
Reviewed the scan-pollution counterexample and the equal-capacity ring isolation counterexample.
Reviewed the two-stage victim workflow for identity stability, dirty preservation, retry, and bounded progress.
proof_review.notes: No proof of policy optimality, lock freedom, starvation freedom, workload generalization, or live-engine correctness is claimed.

evidence: Separated deterministic trace derivations from workload experiments and production conclusions.
Separated offline optimality, exact LRU stack semantics, clock approximation, and adaptive-policy heuristics.
Separated replacement ranking from atomic eligibility and durability correctness.
Audited uses of optimal, proves, invariant, safe, fair, and winner for their explicit model or workload scope.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Policy recommendations require representative measurement and are not presented as mathematical universals.

evidence: The standard-library LRU, clock, and scan-ring calibration executed successfully through the repository verifier.
Five online primary or official destinations returned HTTP 200; the LRU-K DOI resolved correctly but ACM blocked automated full-text retrieval with HTTP 403.
Front matter, section order, local links, ten examples, five exercises, five answers, and snippet expectations passed draft validation apart from the then-pending review record.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live database, concurrent buffer pool, storage device, dirty-page workload, tenant workload, crash, or performance benchmark was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently connects recency, frequency, reuse history, admission, scan resistance, cost, eligibility, concurrency, fairness, and experimental comparison without declaring a universal policy winner.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed exact LRU, clock-sweep, LRU-K, 2Q, adaptive ghost history, scan rings, prefetch, dirty/pinned handling, sharding, quotas, metadata overhead, instrumentation, failure progress, experimentation, canary rollout, and rollback.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet, exact executable comparison, ten distinct worked examples, and five progressive exercises move from trace mechanics through concurrent selection and production policy experimentation.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model do not certify PostgreSQL, InnoDB, any adaptive cache, any concurrent replacement implementation, recovery/writeback protocol, policy benchmark, fairness outcome, or production fitness.
